mpn: RC servo header, 1 x 3 pins, 2.54 mm
description: Header for one RC servo (SG90, MG90S, MG996R…): 1 x 3 male pins at 2.54 mm in the servo plug's order, GND (brown) - V+ (red, middle) - SIGNAL (orange)

datasheet.revision: Tower Pro SG90 mini servo, Rapid 37-1330 sheet (October 2013): 4.8 V operation, 1.8 kg·cm stall torque, 23 x 12.2 x 29 mm

package.name: 1 x 3 pin header, 2.54 mm
package.page: the servo's 3-way 2.54 mm plug: power in the middle so a reversed plug does not reverse the supply

pins.name: VPLUS
pins.description: servo supply (red wire): 4.8-6 V for hobby servos, from a supply able to give the stall current, not from a microcontroller's 3.3 V

pins.name: SIG
pins.description: PWM control (orange, yellow or white wire): a 50 Hz pulse, about 1-2 ms wide, 3.3 V or 5 V logic

parts.rating: our choice: electrolytic, 10 V, near the header (one per few servos)
our choice: series resistor from the controller's PWM pin

inputs.name: gpio
inputs.description: The controller pin it connects to.

notes: A servo draws hundreds of mA moving and much more when stalled: feed V+ from a 5 V supply (or a 2S pack through a 5-6 V regulator) with wide tracks, never through a USB port's 500 mA for several servos, and join its ground with the controller's.
The pulse: 50 Hz, about 1.0 ms one end, 1.5 ms centre, 2.0 ms the other end (many servos accept 0.5-2.5 ms). Many servos at once: a PCA9685 (`PCA9685PW`) makes the pulses over I2C.
Servo plugs (JR / Futaba style) all put V+ in the middle; the outer pins are ground and signal. Mark the GND end on the silkscreen (brown wire).

pins.source: the RC servo plug's wire order (brown ground, red V+ in the middle, orange signal, as Tower Pro labels the SG90's lead); SG90 ratings from the Rapid 37-1330 datasheet
pins.license: pin order (a fact of the connector system), ratings transcribed (facts); descriptions and notes our own

footprint.note: the standard 1 x 3 pin header footprint
